about.title: Personal Injury Help in Redwood City, California
about.longDescription: Redwood City sits along the Peninsula's busiest stretch, and its roads reflect that. In 2025, the city recorded 305 injury collisions, with 412 people hurt and one life lost, according to public records. US-101 runs the length of town, Woodside Road funnels traffic to and from the freeway, and El Camino Real and Middlefield Road carry steady local volume all day. Collision reports tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters, deliveries and weekend traffic converge. If one of those crashes changed your week, your month, or your year, you probably have questions and not much energy to chase answers. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in San Mateo County, and we work on contingency, so you owe us nothing unless your case results in a recovery. Whether you were rear-ended near the Caltrain station downtown, hit while crossing El Camino Real, or injured somewhere other than a road entirely, a conversation costs you nothing. Reaching out early helps, since California limits how long you have to act.

whyChoose.title: Why Redwood City Residents Choose Us

items.title: The clock is real: two years in California
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. Claims against a city, county or state agency can require notice in as little as six months, so getting started early matters.

items.title: Partly at fault? You may still recover
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for a crash on Woodside Road or anywhere else, your recovery is reduced by your percentage, not wiped out.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary California injury cases there is no statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life. We can explain how that applies to your situation.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket to get started
items.desc: Our case review is free, and we work on contingency. You owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Redwood City?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, you have two years from the date of the injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a poorly maintained public sidewalk, you may need to file a formal claim within six months. We can pin down the exact deadline for your facts.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Redwood City?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, the highest-volume corridors are US-101, Woodside Road, El Camino Real and Middlefield Road. Reports also tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are simply counts of where and when collisions were recorded, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so sharing some responsibility does not bar you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by your share of fault, and the rest can still be pursued. Insurers sometimes overstate your fault, which is one reason people choose to talk with us first.

items.question: Do you charge for a consultation, and how does payment work?
items.answer: No, your initial case review is free. We work on contingency, meaning we handle personal injury claims in San Mateo County and you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: What kinds of injury cases do you handle?
items.answer: Car, truck and motorcycle crashes are common, but we also handle pedestrian and bicycle injuries, slip-and-fall incidents, dog bites, and other situations where someone else's negligence caused harm. If you are unsure whether your situation qualifies, reach out anyway. It costs nothing to ask.
